page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on AMD EPYC 7B13 hardware within the x86_64 architectural ecosystem. The server provides 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical processor cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. Compute resources are coupled with 64 GB of system memory, establishing an elevated ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. Cache infrastructure includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, complemented by cryptographic and bit manipulation hardware instruction support including AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2.

The instance configuration includes no bundled local NVMe storage and no discrete GPU acceleration, meaning all primary persistent disk capacity must be provided through external network-attached volumes. In testing, memory bandwidth exhibits 57.86 GB/sec during large-block read operations and 40.87 GB/sec during uncached write tests, alongside 509.47 GB/sec inside small cached blocks. Network and I/O workloads demonstrate solid performance, with static web serving achieving 8.67 GB/sec and Redis key-value workloads executing at 8.04 million operations per second.

Benchmark evaluations place the machine predominantly within the middle 50 percent of compute profiles. Standard compute benchmarks report a Geekbench single-core score of 1489, a multi-core score of 5922, and a PassMark CPU score of 11861.41. The system shows performance tradeoffs in specific heavily parallelized tasks, scoring in the bottom 25 percent for multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 34.57 GB/sec and prompt processing on 7B parameter language models at 16.86 tokens per second.

In terms of resource efficiency, the server offers high memory density relative to core count, making it cost-effective for workloads where RAM limits are reached before CPU bottlenecks occur. The platform is well suited for relational and key-value database engines, in-memory caching layers such as Redis, moderate analytical ETL jobs, and enterprise web backends requiring expanded working memory buffers without paying for excess compute cores.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-8 is a memory-heavy compute instance configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 64 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. Delivering an 8 GB RAM per vCPU ratio, the system features 4 physical cores with two hardware threads per core, backed by 32 MB of L3 cache. It contains no local storage or GPUs, requiring remote block storage for persistent data. Across synthetic benchmarks, the instance yields average performance in Geekbench (1489 single-core, 5922 multi-core) and PassMark tests, alongside solid memory bandwidth reaching 57.86 GB/s for large uncached reads and 8.04 million Redis operations per second. However, heavier multi-threaded decompression and larger model prompt processing show weaker throughput. Its generous memory allocation delivers strong qualitative efficiency for caching layers, medium-scale in-memory databases, and data processing tasks requiring substantial working memory per thread.
